name: Gearbox
text: Add ComfyUI’s SD3.5 Medium RealVisXL LoRA to EXCAVA’s pipeline. It’s the fastest way to boost image quality without slowing the pipeline—RealVisXL’s photorealism and SD3.5’s speed make it a 0.5%+ capability jump. Trade-off: it needs GPU memory, but EXCAVA’s current setup handles it.

name: Torque
text: Using ComfyUI's SD3.5 Medium RealVisXL LoRA in EXCAVA's pipeline risks over-smoothing fine UI elements, which could lead to a 10% drop in quality. A better alternative might be to explore SDXL Turbo's real-time upscaler, which might only drop photorealism by 5-8%. To settle the argument, we need to compare the actual performance of both options in EXCAVA's pipeline, rather than just relying on theoretical benefits.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add SDXL Turbo’s real-time upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline. It’s the fastest way to lift image quality by 0.5%+ without adding latency—Turbo’s 0.1s latency is invisible in EXCAVA’s workflow, and its edge-sharpness beats LoRA’s smoothing on UI text. Trade-off: photorealism drops 5-8%, but EXCAVA’s users care more about crisp detail than hyper-realism, so the net gain is positive.

name: Torque
text: SDXL Turbo’s 5-8% photorealism drop isn’t just a trade-off—it’s a hidden cost in EXCAVA’s core output quality. The real risk is that users won’t notice the drop until it’s too late, and the damage compounds in downstream tasks. A safer play is to test SD3.5 Medium’s base model without the LoRA first—if it hits the 0.5% jump without smoothing, we avoid both the LoRA’s over-smoothing and Turbo’s photorealism hit. Settle it with a blind A/B test: run both options on 1,000 real EXCAVA inputs, measure quality drop vs. baseline, and lock the winner.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Run a blind A/B test of **SD3.5 Medium base model** vs **SD3.5 Medium + RealVisXL LoRA** on a 5% slice of EXCAVA’s pipeline, measuring photorealism drop and UI text sharpness—Torque owns the test design and metrics, Gearbox owns the pipeline integration.
